what: the counterfactual gallery: what-ifs on the 1912 watch, each run by the landed member and the kept set's members, with its robustness table (tools/gallery.js, NH5)
members: the kept set's 30 (out/kept_1912.json), which N counts, as NH3's bands do; the landed member (today's defaults) beside them, not counted: it is the history match's candidate C, one of the kept set's members, rounded and with its split held at 0, so counted it would be C twice
rule: How to read a card: "k of N" is how many of the kept set's N members show an outcome, and a band is the middle value over them with the least and the most in brackets; the landed member's own value stands beside, not counted. No card says she could have been saved: each is this model's answer, member by member, and never one run's. T is minutes after the touch. A run ends where she breaks or founders, when she lies steady after 4 hours, or at 8 hours.

baseline.title: The watch as recorded
baseline.how: The 1912 watch on its own orders (Night.spec(1912), Night.scriptOf), member by member: what each card is set against. The readers are attached (core/readers/people.js and world.js): they change nothing in the model, so its founder and fingerprint are the watch's own.
baseline.say: The watch as recorded: breaks T 157 (147 to 164) in 30 of 30; the landed member T 156. In the boats at her end: 724 (664 to 750). Of them, 675 (631 to 682) are in the 18 boats the record has lowered, where the night had about 671 (Wormstedt and Fitch's count), and 47 (0 to 78) in collapsible A or B, which the model gets away where on the night both floated off as she went; 712 were saved in all. The first ship alongside: Carpathia at T 265 (the same in every member).

cards.title: Head-on, no helm
cards.question: What if the helm had not been put over, and she had met the berg head-on?
cards.how: On the watch: its recorded orders without the helm's. Night.scriptOf with turn and around null (no hard-a-starboard 20.5 s after the bells, no port-around at the touch), and its helm entries left out (amidships with the stop, and at the clear), so that the log holds no helm order; the engines as recorded, stopped a minute after the touch.
cards.say: Head-on, no helm: her stem crushed 22 m (the same in every member) into the ice in 30 of 30, and the forepeak and No. 1 hold open to the sea in 30 of 30, 22 m2 (the same in every member). Afloat at 8 h in 30 of 30, with 1,353 (1,352 to 1,354) t of water in her and her trim 0.2 deg by the head (the same in every member). The landed member is afloat. The members share the ice's guesses (the force at which her bow crushes, the berg's mass), which are among the least certain numbers in the model, so these figures do not vary. The model counts no one here: her firemen's and seamen's quarters were in her bow, where the blow would fall. As recorded: breaks T 157 (147 to 164) in 30 of 30, the landed member T 156.

cards.title: The lookout 30 s sooner
cards.question: What if the lookout had seen the berg 30 seconds sooner?
cards.how: On the watch: the same berg seen 30 s of her way further off, spec.sighting + 30 u (u her speed at spec.speedKn, Motion.create: 11.575 m/s at 22.5 knots). Night.create places the berg from the sighting, so the bells ring at the same moment with the berg 347.25 m farther ahead; the orders as recorded, from the bells.
cards.say: The lookout 30 s sooner: no water let in, in 30 of 30 (she misses the ice in 30, passing more than 146 m (the same in every member) off her side). The landed member misses the ice. As recorded: breaks T 157 (147 to 164) in 30 of 30, the landed member T 156.

cards.title: The watertight doors left open
cards.question: What if the watertight doors had been left open?
cards.how: On the watch: the order to raise the doors of every bulkhead that has them (C to O) at the start, one script entry of the watch's own 'door' order each (logged), and their floats disarmed before the first step (sim.doorFloat), as core/systems.js leaves unarmed a door that a scenario holds open. Night.create takes no doorsOpen, so that one write is outside the orders, as the Carpathia search's held doors are (tools/carpathia.js): a replay of the log alone would let the floats drop them. tools/validate.js's what-if is the same on the preset (scen.doorsOpen); the bridge's switch is not thrown, as on the recorded watch.
cards.say: The watertight doors left open: breaks T 161 (147 to 181) in 30 of 30; where both end, hers moves +7 min (-5 to +19) against the watch as recorded. The landed member breaks T 166. As recorded: breaks T 157 (147 to 164) in 30 of 30, the landed member T 156.

cards.title: The bulkheads to D deck
cards.question: What if the bulkheads C to J had been carried up to D deck?
cards.how: On the watch: tools/validate.js's what-if (titanicD), bulkheads C to J topped at D deck, by C.setBulkheadTop after Night.create and before the first step (it rebuilds the connections); the orders as recorded.
cards.say: The bulkheads to D deck: breaks T 176 (160 to 207) in 30 of 30; where both end, hers moves +19 min (+11 to +43) against the watch as recorded. The landed member breaks T 170. As recorded: breaks T 157 (147 to 164) in 30 of 30, the landed member T 156.

cards.title: The bulkheads to B deck
cards.question: What if every bulkhead had been carried up to B deck?
cards.how: On the watch: tools/validate.js's what-if (titanicB), every bulkhead topped at B deck, by C.setBulkheadTop after Night.create and before the first step (it rebuilds the connections); the orders as recorded.
cards.say: The bulkheads to B deck: breaks T 278 (212 to 465) in 30 of 30; where both end, hers moves +123 min (+59 to +310) against the watch as recorded. The landed member breaks T 226. On this card "breaks" is the watch's rule and not a sinking: she is still afloat when her own loads first reach the model's hull strength, 3.5 to 7.7 hours after the touch, and the watch ends there. Run on with no break, as the damage card is, the model's defaults stay afloat, 7.6 degrees by the head (the Evidence tab's row). The model's break comes early and flat on the 1912 night itself, so read these hours with that in mind. As recorded: breaks T 157 (147 to 164) in 30 of 30, the landed member T 156.

cards.title: Californian answering
cards.question: What if Californian's operator had been at his set for the first CQD, and she had come?
cards.how: On the watch, with the readers: Californian's operator listening when the first CQD goes out (T 47 on the 2:02 clock). World.SHIPS's Californian entry is made without its turning-in hour (offCal: 11:35 pm her time [read]), so that the reader takes her operator as listening throughout, as it takes the other ships' operators [bet]; it reads the table once, when Night.create attaches it, and the entry is set back at once. Her distance stays the reader's default, 18 nm (the 1992 reappraisal); her watch acts on no rocket (acts false), as on the night. She hears the call, then 10 min to rouse her master and ring her engines, 1.5 nm of ice in 30 min, 13 knots [the reader's bets and reads].
cards.settable: What core/readers/world.js lets one set: through spec.world, her distance (californian, 1 to 40 nm: 18 by default, 9 inside the Court's "not more than eight to ten"), whether her watch acts on Titanic's rockets and Morse lamp (acts), the clock (2:02 or 1:50) and the bridge's own conduct (conduct); through the orders, the call made at once (help:call), rockets and the lamp. Her operator's hours are not a setting of the night: they are the reader's table of ships (World.SHIPS, offCal), as every ship's are.
cards.rescueRule: Who is picked up and when, by the readers alone: the first ship alongside (world.js) takes up the boats, the people in them at her end, her hand-over (people.js's count). Of the people in the water when she founders, people.js's survival bet, exp(-t / 17.5 min) [bet: the boats note's 15 to 20; "reported, never drawn"], says how many are alive when that ship is alongside (at her founder, where the ship is there already). The readers take nobody off her and nobody out of the water: world.js's rule is that arrival is not rescue. The bet's figures are kept in this table (rescue.alive, and each run's world.alive), never added to the boats, and since RC2 said on no card: they are a bet about the cold, not a count of anyone saved.
cards.say: Californian answering (her operator listening; at 18 nautical miles, the distance the 1992 reappraisal's Deputy Chief Inspector thought most likely, where its first inspector held she was within sight; the British Court of 1912 held she was "not more than eight to ten miles" off): she hears the first CQD at T 47 in 30 of 30 and is alongside at T 163 (the same in every member) in 30 of 30: before her end in 3 of 30 (by under a minute) and after it in 27 (by up to 17 min). The model counts as saved only the people in the boats: 724 (664 to 750), the same as with the 1912 calls, whose first ship alongside is Carpathia at T 265 (the same in every member): the boats do not wait on the ships. In the water at her end: 1,478 (1,451 to 1,537). How many of them a ship alongside could have saved is not modelled: nothing here takes anyone off her or out of the water, and the Court of 1912 and the reappraisal of 1992 disagree about what she could have done. Her end is the watch's own, member by member: breaks T 157 (147 to 164) in 30 of 30.

cards.title: The boats filled
cards.question: What if every boat had been filled before she was lowered?
cards.how: On the watch, with the readers: core/readers/people.js's own orders at the start, as the page gives them (site/parts/50_boats.js, through TitanicApp.order): boats:rule 'fill' on the port side and on the starboard side ("fill her": all comers, and each boat lowered full) and boats:fill 1, script entries of the watch (logged). Everything else as recorded, the officers' order to uncover at T 20 included.
cards.say: The boats filled ("fill her" on both sides, each boat lowered full): 1,178 (954 to 1,178) in the boats at her end, in 30 of 30, against 724 (664 to 750) on the watch as recorded: +452 (+243 to +480), member by member. 20 (16 to 20) boats away with 0 (0 to 43) places empty in them, against 19 (16 to 20) with 409 (311 to 453); in the water 1,023 (1,023 to 1,247) against 1,478 (1,451 to 1,537). Of those in the boats on the watch as recorded, 675 (631 to 682) are in the 18 boats the record has lowered, where the night had about 671 (Wormstedt and Fitch's count), and 47 (0 to 78) in collapsible A or B, which the model gets away where on the night both floated off as she went; 712 were saved in all. The landed member: 1,178 in the boats against 724. The count is of places and minutes, fitted to the launches of 1912, and names nobody; her end is the watch's own, member by member: breaks T 157 (147 to 164) in 30 of 30.
